observation_summary: The method getCovariances() throws an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when parameters are bound because it iterates over all parameters instead of only the unbound ones, leading to an index mismatch when accessing the Jacobian matrix.
hypothesis: The loop logic in getCovariances() incorrectly uses the total number of parameters (all parameters) to define the iteration bounds and matrix dimensions, while the underlying Jacobian matrix only contains data for the unbound parameters. This causes an out-of-bounds access when the loop index exceeds the size of the unbound parameter set.
prediction: The code will be updated to use the count of unbound parameters (problem.getUnboundParameters().length) instead of the total count (problem.getAllParameters().length) to correctly size the covariance matrix and bound the loops.
experiment_rationale: The bug report explicitly identifies that the loop uses the wrong parameter count (all vs. unbound), which is a procedural logic error in the calculation of the covariance matrix. This is a classic algorithmic mismatch between the data structure (Jacobian) and the iteration strategy.
reasoning_summary: The defect is an algorithmic error where the procedure iterates over the wrong set of parameters (all parameters instead of only unbound ones). This is a procedural logic error in the computation of the covariance matrix, fitting the Algorithm/Method definition perfectly. It is not a missing check (Checking), nor a simple value assignment error (Assignment/Initialization), nor a design-level capability gap (Function/Class/Object).
